questions.answer: Curve with \(x\)-intercepts at \((0,0)\) and \(\left(\tfrac{8}{3},0\right)\), a horizontal point of inflection at \((0,0)\), and a maximum at \((2,16)\).
questions.hint: Write a full structured solution for the teacher to mark.
questions.solution: Curve with \(x\)-intercepts at \((0,0)\) and \(\left(\tfrac{8}{3},0\right)\), a horizontal point of inflection at \((0,0)\), and a maximum at \((2,16)\).

steps.explain: Step 1: Differentiate \(f(x)\) to find the first derivative \(f'(x)\). Set it to \(0\) to locate the stationary points.
Step 2: Differentiate again to find the second derivative \(f''(x)\). This helps classify the stationary points and identify potential points of inflection (POI).
Step 3: Classify the stationary point at \(x = 2\) using the second derivative test, and calculate its \(y\)-coordinate.
Step 4: Classify the stationary point at \(x = 0\). Since \(f'(0) = 0\) and \(f''(0) = 0\), we check for a change in concavity using test points.
steps.work:
$$ \begin{aligned} f''(-1) &= 12(-1)(4 + 3) = -84 < 0 \quad (\text{Concave down}) \\\\ f''(1) &= 12(1)(4 - 3) = 12 > 0 \quad (\text{Concave up}) \end{aligned} $$ 
 Since concavity changes, \((0,0)\) is a horizontal point of inflection.

steps.explain: Step 5: Verify the other potential POI at \(x = 4/3\). We check concavity around \(x = 4/3\).
steps.work:
$$ \begin{aligned} f''(1) &= 12 > 0 \quad (\text{Concave up}) \\\\ f''(2) &= -48 < 0 \quad (\text{Concave down}) \end{aligned} $$ 
 Concavity changes, so \(x = 4/3\) is a non-horizontal POI. \(f(4/3) = 256/27 \approx 9.48\), so the POI is at \((4/3, 256/27)\).

steps.explain: Step 6: Finally, find the \(x\) and \(y\) intercepts to complete the sketch.
steps.work: $$ \begin{aligned} y\text{-intercept: } x=0 &\implies y = 0 \\\\ x\text{-intercepts: } 8x^3 - 3x^4 &= 0 \implies x^3(8-3x) = 0 \implies x = 0, \; x = \dfrac{8}{3} \end{aligned} $$
